To many the system described in these pages may appear new, but it is by no means so, as it was discovered and used by me in 1880, and was then the means of finding out serious defects in a supposed perfect drainage system.

arxiv-2105-12407.title: Recognition of Linear and Star Variants of Leaf Powers is in P
arxiv-2105-12407.creator: Benjamin Bergougnoux, Svein Høgemo, Jan Arne Telle, Martin Vatshelle
arxiv-2105-12407.description: Abstract A k k -leaf power of a tree T T is a graph G G whose vertices are the leaves of T T and whose edges connect pairs of leaves whose distance in T T is at most k k .

arxiv-2112-04862.title: Frobenius Categories over a Triangular Matrix Ring and Comma Categories
arxiv-2112-04862.creator: Dancheng Lu, Panpan Xie
arxiv-2112-04862.description: Abstract . We introduce the dual notions of ℰ ⁡ ( 𝒳 , M , 𝒴 ) \mathcal{E}(\mathcal{X},M,\mathcal{Y}) and ℳ ⁡ ( 𝒳 , M , 𝒴 ) \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{X},M,\mathcal{Y}) , and investigate when they have enough injective objects or projective objects, when they are resolving or co-resolving, and when they are Frobenius categories.

arxiv-2301-02857.title: De Haas - van Alphen Effect under Rotation
arxiv-2301-02857.creator: Shu-Yun Yang, Ren-Da Dong, De-Fu Hou, Hai-Cang Ren
arxiv-2301-02857.description: Abstract We explored the interplay between magnetic field and rotation in the de Hass - van Alphen oscillation. The effect is found to be reduced because of the re-weighting of different states within the same Landau level by rotation energy. The implications of our results on high energy physics and condensed matter physics are speculated.

arxiv-2303-14636.title: Nanostructures for in-situ surface-enhanced Kretschmann-Raether ellipsometry
arxiv-2303-14636.creator: D Mukherjee, B Kalas, S Burger, G Sáfrán, M Serényi, M Fried, P Petrik
arxiv-2303-14636.description: Abstract Spectroscopic ellipsometry is a sensitive and optical model-supported quantitative tool to monitor interfaces. In this work, solid-liquid interfaces are studied using the Kretschmann-Raether configuration for biosensing applications. The interface layers support two purposes simultaneously: (i) chemical suitability for the adsorption of molecules to be detected and (ii) the optical enhancement of the signal to increase the sensitivity.

arxiv-2405-09954.title: Quantization of Cantor-like set on the real projective line
arxiv-2405-09954.creator: A. Hossain, A. Banerjee, Md. N. Akhtar
arxiv-2405-09954.description: Abstract . In this article, an iterated function system (IFS) is considered on the real projective line ℝ ​ ℙ 1 \mathbb{RP}^{1} so that the attractor is a Cantor-like set. Hausdorff dimension of this attractor is estimated. The existence of a probability measure associated with this IFS on ℝ ​ ℙ 1 \mathbb{RP}^{1} is also demonstrated.

arxiv-2409-06506.title: Neural Laplacian Operator for 3D Point Clouds
arxiv-2409-06506.creator: Bo Pang, Zhongtian Zheng, Yilong Li, Guoping Wang, Peng-Shuai Wang
arxiv-2409-06506.description: Abstract . The discrete Laplacian operator holds a crucial role in 3D geometry processing, yet it is still challenging to define it on point clouds. Previous works mainly focused on constructing a local triangulation around each point to approximate the underlying manifold for defining the Laplacian operator, which may not be robust or accurate.

arxiv-2503-15299.title: Inside-Out: Hidden Factual Knowledge in LLMs
arxiv-2503-15299.creator: Zorik Gekhman, Eyal Ben David, Hadas Orgad, Eran Ofek, Yonatan Belinkov, Idan Szpektor, Jonathan Herzig, Roi Reichart
arxiv-2503-15299.description: Abstract This work presents a framework for assessing whether large language models (LLMs) encode more factual knowledge in their parameters than what they express in their outputs. While a few studies hint at this possibility, none have clearly defined or demonstrated this phenomenon.

arxiv-2504-17027.title: Density Functional Theory ToolKit (DFTTK) to Automate First-Principles Thermodynamics via the Quasiharmonic Approximation
arxiv-2504-17027.creator: Nigel Lee En Hew, Luke Allen Myers, Axel van de Walle, Shun-Li Shang, Zi-Kui Liu
arxiv-2504-17027.description:
A 2025 arXiv research paper by Nigel Lee En Hew, Luke Allen Myers, Axel van de Walle, Shun-Li Shang, Zi-Kui Liu. Abstract

The Helmholtz energy is a key thermodynamic quantity representing available energy to do work at a constant temperature and volume. Despite a well-established methodology from first-principles calculations, a comprehensive tool and database are still lacking. To address this gap, we developed an open-source Density Functional Theory Tool Kit (DFTTK), which automates first-principles thermodynamics using the quasiharmonic approximation (QHA) for Helmholtz energy predictions.

arxiv-2505-21504.title: Tunable intertwining via collective excitations
arxiv-2505-21504.creator: András Szabó, R. Chitra
arxiv-2505-21504.description: Abstract The intertwining of multiple order parameters is a widespread phenomenon in equilibrium condensed matter systems, yet its exploration is often hindered by the complexity of real materials. Here, we present a controlled study of intertwined orders in a minimal driven-dissipative quantum-engineered platform.

arxiv-2510-17280.title: Leakage current of high-fluence neutron-irradiated 8” silicon sensors for the CMS Endcap Calorimeter Upgrade
arxiv-2510-17280.creator: E. Zubaroglu
arxiv-2510-17280.description: Abstract The HL-LHC will challenge the detectors with a nearly 10-fold increase in integrated luminosity compared to the previous LHC runs combined, thus the CMS detector will be upgraded to face the higher levels of radiation and the larger amounts of collision data to be collected. The High-Granularity Calorimeter will replace the current endcap calorimeters of the CMS detector.

pmc-10617468.title: Reovirus genomic diversity confers plasticity for protease utility during adaptation to intracellular uncoating
pmc-10617468.creator: Qi Feng Lin, Casey X. L. Wong, Heather E. Eaton, Xiaoli Pang, Maya Shmulevitz
pmc-10617468.description: Mammalian orthoreoviruses (reoviruses) infect many mammals and provide a safe model to study enteric viruses. Knowledge of reoviruses is derived from prototypic lab strains, notably T1L and T3D. Based on these prototypic strains, reoviruses can efficiently utilize gut or lysosomal proteases for uncoating and penetration into host cytoplasm.

pmc-11290554.title: Nursing students' perceptions of interaction in a multiplayer virtual reality simulation: A qualitative descriptive study
pmc-11290554.creator: Niina Piispanen, Elina Haavisto, Linda Hublin, Riikka Ikonen, Jaana‐Maija Koivisto
pmc-11290554.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). AimTo describe nursing students' perceptions of interaction in a multiplayer virtual reality (MPVR) simulation.DesignA qualitative descriptive study.MethodsSecond‐semester nursing students (n = 24) participated in pairs in MPVR simulations and semi‐structured interviews. Data were analysed deductively and inductively.ResultsFour types of interaction in a MPVR simulation were identified: interaction between the students, interaction between the student and the virtual environment (VE), interaction between the student and the virtual patient (VP), and interaction between the student and the simulation facilitator.

pmc-11508521.title: Increased Prevalence of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder in Individuals with Selective Immunoglobulin A Deficiency: A Nationwide Case–Control Study
pmc-11508521.creator: Eugene Merzon, Reem Farag, Shai Ashkenazi, Eli Magen, Iris Manor, Abraham Weizman, Ilan Green, Avivit Golan-Cohen, Akim Genshin, Shlomo Vinker, Ariel Israel
pmc-11508521.description: Background: Selective Immunoglobulin A Deficiency (SIgAD) is one of the most prevalent immunodeficiencies, characterized by an increased risk of mucosal infections. Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) is among the most common neurodevelopmental disorders and is associated with significantly higher rates of various infectious diseases, white blood cell abnormalities, and considerable morbidity.

pmc-12405085.title: Identification of hotspots of crop wild relatives in Germany to promote their in situ conservation in a network of genetic reserves
pmc-12405085.creator: Maria Bönisch, Vera Senße, Thomas Engst, Alica Sander, Diethart Matthies, Eckhard Jedicke, Nadine Bernhardt
pmc-12405085.description: BackgroundCrop wild relatives (CWR) represent a valuable resource for ensuring food security. Although they are negatively affected by the loss of habitats due to climate change and land use change, they are underrepresented in conservation programmes. The establishment of genetic reserve (GR) networks has been put forward as an approach to protect CWR.

pmc-12689582.title: A scoping review of current trends of multisectoral collaborations for health within the education, agriculture, and environment sectors in Anglophone Africa
pmc-12689582.creator: Ugenyi Victoria Iloabachie, Maureen Nwokorie, Casmir Mbaegbu, Kingsley Ude, Chinyere Ojiugo Mbachu, Obinna Onwujekwe
pmc-12689582.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundIn Anglophone Africa, addressing the double disease burden of disease requires coordinated action across both the health and non-health sectors. Despite the existence of policies advocating this multisectoral collaborations, implementation remains limited and inconsistent across the continent.

pmc-12703958.title: Parental policy-related worry and low-income families' well-being in the context of U.S. executive orders: A cross-sectional analysis
pmc-12703958.creator: Jiying Ling, Lorraine B Robbins, Kenneth Resnicow
pmc-12703958.description: Objective This study examined the relationship between parental worry about current U.S. executive orders, particularly regarding access to federal assistance programs, and family well-being. Methods Cross-sectional data collected in April–May 2025 from 140 low-income parents in the Midwestern U.S. were analyzed. Parents and preschoolers were non-randomly recruited from Head Start organizations.

pmc-12720104.title: Development and validation of a nursing practice scale for supporting fertility preservation decision-making in women with cancer
pmc-12720104.creator: Mikako Yoshihara, Kazuaki Tanabe, Chie Teramoto, Hiroyuki Sawatari, Ruxin Lei, Hisae Nakatani
pmc-12720104.description: ObjectiveWith increasing attention to fertility preservation (FP) among women with cancer, nursing support for FP decision-making remains insufficient and lacks standardization. Nurses often face challenges such as limited knowledge, inconsistent practices, and the absence of structured decision-support frameworks. This study aimed to develop and psychometrically validate a scale to assess nursing practices that support FP decision-making in women with cancer.

pmc-12804587.title: Evaluation of a human 3D multicellular hepatic spheroid model as a platform for studying hepatic transporters
pmc-12804587.creator: Mattie Hartauer, Henry Ho, Meimei Wan, William A Murphy, Jacqueline B Tiley, John K Fallon, Colin E Bishop, Kim L R Brouwer
pmc-12804587.description: There is growing demand for improved in vitro liver models to better predict in vivo pharmacology, specifically drug disposition mediated by hepatic transporters and assessment of transporter-mediated drug interaction risk. While 2D sandwich-cultured human hepatocytes (SCHH) remain valuable, they are limited to short-term use due to hepatocyte de-differentiation and absence of non-parenchymal cells.

pmc-13181234.title: Effects of seed packaging, storage conditions, and durations on seed quality of open-pollinated maize (Zea mays L.) varieties in Ethiopia
pmc-13181234.creator: Kedir Oshone Hussen, Karta Kaske Kalsa
pmc-13181234.description: ObjectiveThis study investigates the combined effects of storage environments and packaging materials on the seed quality of open-pollinated maize (Zea mays L.) (OPM) varieties intended for planting purposes after long-term storage.MethodsMelkassa-2, Melkassa-4, and Melkassa-6Q seeds were stored under cold and ambient storage conditions.

pmc-13420485.title: Bone Mineral Density Loss After Kidney Transplantation: Metabolic Determinants, Diagnostic Approaches, and Preventive Strategies
pmc-13420485.creator: Clemens Untersulzner, Markus Pirklbauer, Pieter Evenepoel, Heinz Zoller, Andreas Kronbichler
pmc-13420485.description: Mineral and bone disease (MBD) is a frequent complication after solid organ transplantation. The rapid decline in bone mineral density (BMD) during the first year after kidney transplantation reflects complex interactions between immunosuppressive therapy, metabolic factors and pre-existing chronic kidney disease (CKD)-MBD.
